reference: Bash metadata plus GNU cat on fixed private offline roster snapshots. Only cluster members is invoked for operation coverage; source dispatch and documentation specify that it streams a local snapshot without any socket/listener. Protocol and lifecycle operations need a future disposable VM with independent peers.
coverage: GNU cat parity for small offline roster streaming, binary/blank/unterminated input, repeated calls, empty snapshots and temporary relative directory assignments.
Custom parse contract for timeout endpoints without any network verb.
Deferred membership initialization, joins, protocol, listener lifecycle and state recovery.
exclusions: Offline members streaming establishes file-interface parity only. It does not establish network membership, authentication, key handling, listener or kernel behavior.
All network, listener-start/stop and membership mutation operations remain deferred with explicit future VM prerequisites.

cases.purpose: GNU Bash type -t reports the builtin category without invoking the cluster implementation.
GNU Bash help can resolve the cluster synopsis and documentation using builtin metadata only.
Verify seed startup, ephemeral loopback port selection, generated key and node IDs, initial one-member roster, private file modes, and listener ownership by a persistent shell.
cases.reason: No init has ever run; one candidate shell in a per-side script suffices.

cases.purpose: Verify a peer joins the seed using its key file, receives the seed cluster ID, and rejects a different valid key without changing either roster.
cases.reason: No lifecycle operation is executed; two candidate shells and an independent BLAKE2b oracle can run inside one per-side script.

cases.purpose: Verify three-peer roster convergence after joins and leaves, heartbeat refresh, peer expiry, and leaf disconnection after seed loss.
cases.reason: No multi-peer run exists; three candidate shells in one per-side script are feasible within the 60 s case limit using short timeouts.

cases.purpose: Verify ping by both node ID and numeric loopback endpoint, plus unknown-node and non-protocol timeout failures.
cases.reason: No ping runs; the python3 protocol peer can validate and answer on loopback.

cases.purpose: Verify malformed, truncated, oversized, wrong-key, invalid-count, and invalid-node packets do not add members or prevent a later valid ping.
cases.reason: No listener is ever started; the python3 injector and oracle can run in the same per-side script.

cases.purpose: Verify leave is repeatable, removes owned state while preserving unrelated fixture files, notifies the seed, and cleans up the listener when its owning shell exits.
cases.reason: No lifecycle run exists; owner-exit is observable by the per-side script waiting on its own child shell and checking the recorded listener PID and port.

cases.purpose: Verify private-directory checks, 0600 state files, key-file syntax, lock collision behavior, atomic snapshot recovery, stale state cleanup, and preservation of unrelated files.
cases.reason: Only offline snapshot reading is executed; all state-management obligations need init/listener runs, which are possible in a per-side VM script.

cases.purpose: Validate init/join/ping arguments and timeout handling in lifecycle contexts; the offline members parser is covered separately.
cases.reason: Lifecycle verbs never run; a per-side script in the VM can invoke them on loopback and inspect the state directory and listening sockets.

cases.purpose: Read a fixed private roster byte-for-byte against GNU cat without initializing membership, opening sockets or starting a listener.
cases.script:
mkdir state
printf '%s
' '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef 127.0.0.1:1234' 'fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210 127.0.0.1:2345' > state/members
if [[ $(type -t cluster) == builtin ]]; then
 BASHCLUSTER_STATE_DIR=state cluster members
else
 cat state/members
fi

cases.purpose: Offline roster streaming retains NUL, blank records and the unterminated final record across repeated calls; no membership protocol is exercised.
cases.script:
mkdir state
printf 'one\000two\n\nlast' > state/members
for repeat in 1 2; do
 if [[ $(type -t cluster) == builtin ]]; then BASHCLUSTER_STATE_DIR=state cluster members; else cat state/members; fi
done

cases.purpose: Switch relative snapshot directories with temporary environment assignments and accepted timeout endpoints; stream exact bytes against GNU cat.
cases.script:
mkdir first second
printf A > first/members
: > second/members
for setting in 'first 50' 'second 5000' 'first 5000'; do
 read -r dir timeout <<< "$setting"
 if [[ $(type -t cluster) == builtin ]]; then BASHCLUSTER_STATE_DIR="$dir" BASHCLUSTER_TIMEOUT_MS="$timeout" cluster members; else cat "$dir/members"; fi
done

cases.purpose: Reject out-of-range timeout values before opening even a private roster; these parse-only operations cannot enter a network verb.
cases.script:
for timeout in 49 5001; do
 rc=0; BASHCLUSTER_STATE_DIR=state BASHCLUSTER_TIMEOUT_MS="$timeout" cluster members || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
done
printf 'invalid timeout rejected\n'
